title: Birthday girl Lovlina makes history with gold, joins Mary Kom in elite club
content: Lovlina Borgohain made history by clinching a gold medal at the Asian Games, becoming just the second Indian woman boxer to achieve this feat. She delivered an impressive performance, sweeping the finals against China's Ziyi Bao with a perfect 5-0 score. This triumph comes after her silver medal in the last Asian Games, where her journey was highlighted by a semifinal win against world champion Natalya Bogdanova.

title: Ambulance stopped for CM Himanta’s convoy: 4 Assam cops suspended
content: Four traffic cops in Silchar were suspended for briefly halting an ambulance to clear a path for CM Himanta Biswa Sarma. The incident occurred while attempting to transport a critically ill patient to the hospital. Sarma later apologized to the family and stated that emergency medical care should take priority over VIP movement. He also emphasized the importance of implementing guidelines governing convoy procedures.

title: Ford CEO Jim Farley makes clear distinction of the jobs that AI cannot replace
content: Ford's CEO Jim Farley emphasized that artificial intelligence will complement skilled trades workers, assuring that roles requiring hands-on skills and practical judgment are safe despite AI advancements. He pointed out that fostering trust is crucial for the successful collaboration between workers and AI. Additionally, he noted the merging roles of tradespeople and engineers in contemporary manufacturing, showcasing Ford's evolution in job functions to adapt to technology.

title: Property value rose before registration; ITAT scraps Rs 11.35 lakh tax on buyer
content: Under Section 56(2)(x), there is applicable taxation of such a difference in the buyer's hands if the stamp duty value of the property is higher than the purchase consideration by more than the greater of Rs 50,000 or 10% of the consideration.  Here, the difference of approximately Rs 22.71 lakh exceeded 10% of the agreed purchase price of Rs 1.23 crore.

title: Taiwan to receive first new F-16 Viper jets from US
content: Taiwan is gearing up to strengthen its aerial defenses with the arrival of its first two F-16V fighter jets, marking a significant step in a broader U.S. agreement for 66 aircraft worth roughly $8 billion. These upgraded jets will come equipped with cutting-edge avionics and radar systems, expanding Taiwan's fleet to over 200 F-16s. Despite past delays, more jets are anticipated to arrive before the year's end, amidst ongoing U.S.

title: Asian Games: Kumkum Mohod, Dhiraj Bommadevara win mixed recurve team silver
content: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara secured a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event at the Asian Games. The Indian pair fought back from a 0-4 deficit against China's Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li, but lost 3-5. Earlier in the semifinals, they staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Japan's Nanami Asakuno and Junya Nakanishi. India's women's recurve team also won gold by defeating South Korea for the first time.

title: Jack Johnson’s Hawaii farm harvested over 40,000 pounds of produce in six years
content: Kōkua Hawaiʻi Foundation acquired unused farmland on Oʻahu in 2019 to create an educational resource. Over six years, more than 40,000 pounds of produce were harvested while 2,200 students participated in learning experiences. The farm emphasizes ecological education, agroforestry, and understanding local food systems through hands-on activities. Community involvement plays a significant role in maintaining the farm through regular volunteer opportunities.

title: Scientists tracked deep-sea dye; canyon water rose 100 metres a day
content: Researchers utilized fluorescein dye in the Rockall Trough to study deep ocean water upwelling. They measured rapid upward movement reaching about 125 metres per day, significantly faster than average estimates. This study provides direct observations of upwelling in submarines canyons, offering insights into ocean circulation dynamics. Findings suggest underwater topography plays a crucial role in deep-water circulation processes. Future research aims to explore similar processes in different submarine canyon settings.

title: Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund commits more than $25 million to Pacific ocean conservation
content: Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund has announced more than $25 million in new ocean conservation grants across five Pacific nations. The funding will support marine protection and sustainable management across more than 625,000 square miles. The latest awards bring the fund’s Pacific commitment to $63.3 million of its planned $100 million.

title: Utah removes 17 million tons of radioactive waste from beside Colorado River
content: The Moab Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action Project has efficiently relocated 17 million tons of waste from the riverbank. Following rail transportation, teams are actively monitoring groundwater contamination levels. Upcoming efforts will also involve excavating contaminated soil near the original tailings site. The objective is to guarantee long-term safety and stability for local residents and the ecosystem. Ultimately, regrading and revegetating the area will be crucial in preventing future erosion.

title: Mumbai delivery worker caught urinating in society lift; CCTV video goes viral
content: A food delivery worker was filmed urinating in the elevator of Akshay Co-operative Housing Society in Mumbai. Residents noticed a foul smell and checked the CCTV footage, which confirmed the incident. The footage went viral on social media, raising community concerns. Following this, the housing society filed a police complaint against the delivery worker. Also, residents have questioned the verification process for delivery personnel entering their homes.

title: 'Mohammad' Deepak arrested for ‘assaulting’ trader over FB comment on Ujjain mosque
content: Deepak Kumar, known for defending an elderly Muslim shopkeeper, was arrested for assaulting a trader. The altercation arose from an online comment regarding a mosque demolition in Ujjain. Kumar allegedly confronted Sanjeev Tonk over a disputed Facebook post. Police intervened to prevent a law and order situation following the incident at Tonk's shop. Kumar is set to be presented before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate under relevant legal provisions.

title: 'Unsuitable for service': 2 Gujarat IAS officers forced into retirement
content: The Gujarat government has taken disciplinary action leading to the compulsory retirement of two IAS officers. Kankipati Rajesh faces ongoing corruption and money-laundering investigations by CBI and ED since 2022. Gaurav Dahiya was suspended in 2019 over allegations of misconduct, including bigamy and cheating. Both officers were deemed unsuitable for service based on their reviewed records by the Department of Personnel and Training.

title: India’s Asian Games gold slide: 20 of 28 Hangzhou titles already lost
content: At the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, India has witnessed a notable drop in gold medals, plummeting from 28 in Hangzhou to merely 10 this time around. Key defeats were recorded in shooting, athletics, and team events, stirring concerns about future prospects. However, the men's hockey and cricket finals still present a chance to hold onto some glory, prompting reflection on how India can reclaim its previous success in sports.

title: 'Proud of our Mumbai boy': Netizens hail flydubai hero pilot, seek Ashok Chakra

Residents from Ghatkopar are expressing pride as they share his background and achievements. Many shared his 2025 podcast discussing the importance of having doctors on flights in emergencies.

title: 2 days on, Ph-3 chaos throws up design flaws in entire Barapullah
content: Delhi's recent opening of the Barapullah Phase III corridor has resulted in significant traffic congestion for commuters. Thousands of drivers expected a quick journey but faced extended delays beyond two hours. Traffic Police are examining the corridor's design and lane configurations to improve flow. They are considering temporary measures such as barricades and traffic regulation adjustments. Further analysis includes addressing navigation app routing to better manage traffic conditions.

title: India's defence export milestone: Akash air defence missile enters Central Asia
content: India's Akash air defence missile system has been successfully exported to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. This follows the initial export to Armenia, marking significant international expansion. The Akash system is designed to protect areas from aerial threats and has a proven operational record. Additionally, the Indian armed forces are placing more orders and potential international demand is expected. The growth of India's defence exports reflects its advancing missile production capabilities.

title: ‘If India won a medal, we owe it to her’: Captain Swayams on Savitha's heroics

After kicking things off with Srinath Narayanan and India's silver-winning Open team, we turn to Swayams Mishra, captain of the bronze-winning women's team. In an exclusive interaction, the 34-year-old opens up about his first full stint as captain, the difficult decision-making around Vaishali, Savitha Shri's match-winning impact, and much more.

title: Gandhi Jayanti: Are NSE, BSE closed for trading on October 2?
content: Stock trading will be halted on October 2, 2026, in observance of Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti. Both the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange will be closed for the day, along with the Multi Commodity Exchange. Investors have faced declines for four consecutive sessions, impacted by foreign selling and escalating crude oil prices. The trading schedule will also be affected by the upcoming Dussehra and Diwali holidays.

title: Prove you are Indian, Calcutta HC tells SIR-deleted ‘Bangladeshi’

The court expressed concerns about the husband's capability to demonstrate his Indian nationality during ongoing investigations. Detained since August 31 on suspicions of illegal immigration from Bangladesh, his legal team contends that the detention is unjustified, as he has not been formally charged. Authorities have mandated the submission of his citizenship documentation.

title: From modest Madeira home to $30M palace: Cristiano Ronaldo's journey
content: Cristiano Ronaldo grew up in a small home in Madeira, sharing his space with three siblings. He pursued his football talent, moving to Lisbon to join Sporting CP at 12 years old. After reaching prominence in football, he built a mansion in Cascais, valued between €30 million and €35 million. Despite its luxury, he chose to sell it soon after completion to seek more privacy.

title: Uttar Pradesh teen kills his mother for opposing sex change
content: In Lucknow, a 17-year-old allegedly killed his 42-year-old mother following an argument about gender-affirming surgery. The minor had been living as a female and wanted to undergo surgery. An altercation reportedly arose when the mother advised against the procedure. The teenager attacked her with an iron wrench, resulting in fatal injuries. He subsequently informed the police about the incident himself.

title: India-US trade deal not imminent, PM Modi-Trump may hold another call soon: US trade rep

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer revealed that teams are actively working through residual challenges. Union Minister Piyush Goyal engaged in talks with Greer during the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting to expedite the deal. A forthcoming call between PM Modi and President Trump is likely to evaluate the progress.

title: Gulf oil infrastructure at risk as US rushes Patriot missiles to Saudi Arabia, Qatar

This move aims to protect critical oil and gas facilities against potential Iranian attacks. Concerns were raised by Saudi and Qatari leaders regarding Iran's potential retaliation amidst escalating tensions. Moreover, the Pentagon is increasing military presence in the Middle East, deploying additional warships and troops.

title: OpenAI fires 3 researchers as AI safety concerns intensify across tech industry

At least two of them worked on AI safety and alignment, areas focused on making advanced AI systems behave safely and follow human instructions. "We have parted ways with three individuals," OpenAI told news agency AFP in a statement.

title: Gold medal secured! India’s women recurve archers defeat South Korea in final

The final was a nail-biter, with both teams demonstrating exceptional prowess amidst blustery weather. This landmark win comes after a thrilling semifinal against China, underscoring the team's exceptional talent and tenacity.

title: Simi Singh: An Ireland dream, a life-threatening detour and the journey home
content: Simranjit Singh a.k.a Simi Singh left left India in 2006 to pursue hotel management, found an unexpected second career in cricket, played for Ireland at the 2022 T20 World Cup and then survived acute liver failure. Now, after his wife donated part of her liver to save him, Simi Singh has returned home to Mohali, bringing a remarkable 20-year journey to an end. Yet, his association with cricket will continue: he's opened an academy, where he is honing young talent.

title: Oil prices soar to $103 per barrel again as Middle East supply concerns intensify

content: the Cockroach Janta Party is set to hold a “Jail Bharo Andolan” against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar . the two urged commuters and residents to gather at the protest venue . dipke was seen posing with an auto driver .

title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Panna villagers standing in water for last 20 days
content: protesters brave rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities . amit Bhatnagar, jai Kisan Sangathan leader, was arrested on a hunger strike . the agitation is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain and waterlogging .

title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
content: goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents . three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others are currently based outside India . the office of the goa electoral officer said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll .

title: More than 1 million bats emerge from lava tubes on Ted Turner's ranch
content: more than 1 million free-tailed bats can emerge from ancient lava tubes . spectacle takes place at armendaris Ranch, a 362,885-acre property in south-central new Mexico along the Rio Grande . the current Ted Turner Reserves experience says over 1 million can rush from the caves at sunset .
